recipe.notes:
Serving: vllm serve zeroentropy/zembed-1-embedding --runner pooling --convert embed
--max-model-len 32768, on the unmodified vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0 image, no plugin.
1. Runner/convert are explicit for robustness: at v0.31.0 a bare serve already resolves this
   checkpoint to pooling + embed, because the sentence-transformers modules.json wins over the
   generative Qwen3ForCausalLM architecture and convert falls through to embed for a pooling
   runner on a CausalLM arch. The flags equal what auto resolves; they pin the intent.
2. pooler_config stays empty on purpose: the engine reads modules.json + 1_Pooling/config.json
   (last-token pooling, L2 normalize) from the checkpoint itself, and the embed conversion
   normalizes server-side. There is no chat template on the serving path: the prompts are
   literal client-side text, the checkpoint's own chat_template.jinja stays unused, and
   serve.chat_template is null. Never route this model through /v2/embed with input_type: that
   route renders chat messages through the Qwen3 chat template, a different token sequence
   (measured when the recipe was written). The engine never imports the remote module, so trust_remote_code is false.
3. The render is prefix + content + suffix, declared as data in client.template: the query and
   document prompts come from config_sentence_transformers.json, and the suffix (the im_end
   marker plus a newline) is appended by the checkpoint's remote code (modeling_zembed.py:13,
   ZembedTransformer.tokenize). The suffix is load-bearing: the pooler reads the last token, so
   it is the template's trailing fixed segment and the anchor the budget reserves. The template
   writes specials by name ({special:im_start}, {special:im_end}), never literally.
4. Budget: the whole rendered prompt is capped at 32768 tokens (sentence_bert_config.json
   max_seq_length, the same number as serve.max_model_len). on_overflow: cut trims the content
   spans only, after reserving every fixed template token, and re-attaches the frame, so the
   anchor survives every cut (docs/how-to/add-a-model.md, "Anchors"). The engine never truncates: vLLM
   defaults to no truncation and 400s over-length inputs, so the client-side cut (the merged
   product's embedding client fitting every request to the declared budget,
   rcp_ndcg.data.preprocess.fit) is the only one. Per-shape query caps (whether
   query_max_tokens applies): no separate query cap exists in the referent - the reference cuts
   queries and documents alike at 32768 tokens - so query_max_tokens is not declared and both
   shapes draw on max_tokens.
5. The reference is the model's published path verbatim and never ports the client's cut
   (docs/how-to/add-a-model.md): over-cap, the remote tokenize's whole-prompt right cut drops the
   pooled suffix token, while the served side keeps the anchor
   by the declared client cut. The reference's over-cap cut therefore differs from the client's
   AND drops the anchor, so the recipe declares reference.known_deviations: [anchor_drop_over_cap]:
   over-cap pairs ride the non-gating table and stage 2 gates only the under-cap rows.
6. Dimensions: 2560 only, and MRL is declared (owner decision 39). The card's smaller sizes
   (1280..40) come from projections.safetensors - six chained learned F32 matrices
   (4,368,000 params; params x 4 B + 456 B header = 17,472,456 B exactly) - not Matryoshka
   slices, so the client head is mrl_kind: projection with mrl_projection.source
   (hf://zeroentropy/zembed-1-embedding@<revision>/projections.safetensors; the file's tensor
   names are their target widths) and mrl_dims [1280, 640, 320, 160, 80, 40]. The checkpoint
   declares no matryoshka_dimensions, so vLLM refuses a dimensions parameter outright; do not
   set client.dimensions for this model - the client-side mrl_dim is the one cut, and a run
   selects k from the declared set (the GPU wave gates each k).
7. Reference environment (the reference's own python, per requirements-reference.txt):
   torch>=2.0, transformers>=4.51 (Qwen3's floor; the image's transformers serves it), numpy,
   and sentence-transformers>=5.3,<5.4 -- the last line whose encode calls the remote
   tokenize; from 5.4.0 the preprocess-first pipeline bypasses the tokenize-only remote module
   and silently drops the suffix. 5.1.x would require transformers<5 and could not reuse the
   image's transformers (>=5.10.4,<5.18.0 at v0.31.0); 5.3.x accepts it, so the reference venv
   (--system-site-packages over the image) installs only sentence-transformers. The reference loads the checkpoint with trust_remote_code=True (the model card's
   usage); the served engine never imports that code.
8. Status unverified. The render was proved token-exact on CPU (8/8 cases measured when the
   recipe was written, constants bound to the checkpoint's config files). The first GPU wave
   measured every served vector differing from the card's (cosine 0.08-0.4 on all 68 vectors,
   with the renders equal) and the engine hanging at exactly max_model_len. The root cause was
   the reference environment, not the served pooling path: the node's shared reference venv
   installed an unbounded sentence-transformers, and 6.1.0's preprocess-first pipeline drops the
   suffix (min cosine 0.081024 over the same 68 vectors), while under the pinned 5.3.x line the
   same comparison is min 0.999203; the direct transformers path and the card's encode_query
   agree with the recorded engine vector at 0.999884-0.999890. The served path is correct, the
   recipe now opts into the pooling-full-context patch for the hang, and E2 re-measures stage 2
   under the pinned reference environment.
sources: https://huggingface.co/zeroentropy/zembed-1-embedding/raw/cf13c81f3274394053d166740294f7eea4586f7a/README.md (the card's projection sentence at line 33: 'The model supports flexible dimension projections (2560, 1280, 640, 320, 160, 80, 40)')

projections.safetensors at the pinned revision (the safetensors header read at cf13c81f...): six F32 tensors named by their target widths, 1280 [2560,1280], 640 [1280,640], 320 [640,320], 160 [320,160], 80 [160,80], 40 [80,40] -- the chain the client's mrl_projection applies, widest first, to reach k
vllm/config/model.py:1242-1244 at the v0.31.0 tag (db9527a) - the checkpoint's sentence-transformers modules.json resolves the pooling runner before the architecture registry
vllm/config/model.py:1307-1311 at the v0.31.0 tag (db9527a) - convert falls through to embed for a pooling runner on a CausalLM arch

vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:991-1068 - the pooler settings (last-token, normalize) are read from modules.json + 1_Pooling/config.json, so pooler_config stays empty; verified at both revisions (v0.31.0 tag: get_pooling_config at :982)
vllm/model_executor/layers/pooler/seqwise/poolers.py:97-108 - last-token pooling with server-side normalize for the embed conversion (verified at both revisions)

vllm/renderers/params.py:469-476 - the engine's right-truncation slice; :485-509 - the no-truncation default 400s over-length inputs, so the client cut is the only truncation (verified at both revisions)
vllm/pooling_params.py:175 - a checkpoint without matryoshka_dimensions refuses a dimensions parameter (verified at both revisions)
vllm/entrypoints/pooling/base/protocol.py:218 - /v1/embeddings add_special_tokens defaults to true (verified at both revisions)

vllm/entrypoints/pooling/embed/io_processor.py:530-536 - /v2/embed with input_type renders chat messages through the checkpoint's chat template; this recipe never routes there (verified at both revisions)
